patches.old:
The glorious man was lord of the whole tower. When he finished, he called the shepherd. He handed over all the rejected stones lying beside the tower and told him,[a]

2. “Clean these stones carefully. Put into the tower’s building those that can fit with the rest. Throw the ones that do not fit far away from the tower.”

3. After giving these orders, he left the tower with everyone who had come with him.[b] The virgins stood around the tower and guarded it.

4. I asked the shepherd, “How can these rejected stones go back into the tower’s building?” He asked, “Do you see these stones?” I said, “I see them, sir.” He said, “I will cut most of them and put them into the building. They will fit with the others.”

5. I asked, “Sir, how can they fill the same space after being cut down?” He answered, “The small ones will go inside the building. The larger ones will go outside and hold them together.”

6. He said, “Let us go. In two days we will return, clean these stones and put them into the building. Everything around the tower must be cleaned. The master might come suddenly, find it dirty and be displeased. Then these stones will not go into the tower’s building, and the master will think I have been negligent.”

7. Two days later we came to the tower. He said, “Let us examine all the stones and see which can go into the building.” I said, “Sir, let us examine them.”

translation:
  text: 'When the glorious man, the lord of the whole tower, had finished this, he
    called the shepherd and handed over to him all the stones lying beside the tower
    that had been rejected from the building. He said to him,[a]


    2. “Carefully clean these stones and put into the building of the tower those
    that can fit with the rest. Throw those that do not fit far away from the tower.”


    3. After giving these orders to the shepherd, he left the tower with everyone
    who had come with him.[b] The virgins stood around the tower, guarding it.


    4. I said to the shepherd, “How can these stones go back into the building of
    the tower after being rejected?” He answered me, “Do you see these stones?” “I
    see them, sir,” I said. “I will cut most of these stones,” he said, “and put them
    into the building. They will fit with the other stones.”


    5. “Sir,” I said, “how can they fill the same space after being cut down?” He
    answered me, “Those found to be small will be put inside the building. The larger
    ones will be placed outside and hold them together.”


    6. After telling me this, he said, “Let us go, and after two days let us return,
    clean these stones and put them into the building. Everything around the tower
    must be cleaned, in case the master suddenly comes, finds the area around the
    tower dirty and becomes displeased. Then these stones will not go into the building
    of the tower, and I will seem negligent to the master.”


    7. After two days we came to the tower. He said to me, “Let us examine all the
    stones and see which can go into the building.” I said to him, “Sir, let us examine
    them.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: “Lord” describes the glorious man’s authority over the tower; “master” later
      renders despotes. “Sir” is Hermas’s address to the shepherd. The draft keeps
      the roles distinct without treating every occurrence as the same named divine
      title. The later explanation identifies the glorious man as the Son of God.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “After giving these orders to the shepherd, he left the tower” is a bar-marked
      supplement in the working Greek, absent from Athos as reported. It is retained
      with its versional basis visible. The two-day interval and the shepherd’s concern
      about seeming negligent remain explicit.
